entries.defect: Bound: at most 1 concurrently submitted or running cloud author (counted from submission, not branch visibility), plus at most 1 completed successor waiting for acceptance. Resolution against A's 2: the only measured cloud cycle (1440) landed 1.3 h after submission while acceptance-only game points averaged 3.05 h (1414 2.0, 1432 3.5, 1333 5.8, 1297 0.9), so one author already outproduces acceptance ~2.3x; a second author only lengthens the ready queue, and every branch that waited >1 day (1297, 1333, 1414, 1432) needed post-sync rework, wasting credit that expires 05.11.2026. Raise to 2 only if the measured cycle shows an acceptance window opening with no ready successor.

KEEP POOL_CAP 3 and commission-guard's existing LAND/PARK remedies; slot math is 1 branch in acceptance + 1 cloud/ready + the open 1347. 1347 (idle since 21.10) is parked through the existing park record only if the measured cycle shows its slot blocking a commissioning; the drain itself is 1443's work and is not repeated.

Switch-over resolved: write the numeric bound now and run the first post-1443 cycle under it; since the runbook already permitted cloud authoring during acceptance and only lacked a number (A31), that cycle is both the 1443 baseline B asks for and the trial. From the first point after 1444: at the start of each acceptance window, if no completed successor waits, commission the next ready, file-disjoint queue point via the existing cloud-switch/author-delegate path and declare it in batch-in-flight; file-disjointness is checked with the existing independentOpenPoints against every occupied lane. The bound is procedural because commission-guard counts branches, not sessions, so no new guard is possible or needed.

KEEP cloud-switch ON and lane-routing default for the measured cycle (vendor role and execution locality are different axes, and A28 shows the local main-chain authors were fallbacks after 4/4 failed non-main starts). The cycle records for each authoring delegation where it ran; if a delegation runs locally while the switch is ON, fix that decision in author-delegate with Vitest, after reading the complete (untruncated) code.

Bound: 1 local heavy job (browser suite, unit gate, picture check or local author running Vitest) and 0 other local agents during acceptance windows, draining or checkpointing already-running local authors first; outside windows at most 1 local author alongside cloud work. Derivation: 15 GB RAM with 12 GB available and swap in use, the 23.10 suite-memory-wall record, the ~20 % suite slowdown under load, and the single overlapped-suite sample (23.10 04:59/05:02Z) where both runs went red.

Section re-runs: after one repeat of an unchanged SHA, section, backend and failure signature, stop re-running and diagnose (a relevant commit or a recorded changed condition reopens the budget). Repeats cost 8.2 h; 1405 had 27 completed runs for 158.4 min and 1404 about 20 repeats.

Red-charging: when a red is already charged to an open point and main is unchanged for that section, reuse the recorded main run instead of re-proving it on main (1.4 h measured). Procedural change; Vitest only if a script makes this decision.

Coalesce retrospective-fingerprint, guide-attest and queue-rank refreshes into one bookkeeping commit/push per point boundary, keeping required user-order publication receipts. Resolution against A's once-per-day: the rule demanding the refresh is not located in the material and A's own risk notes guards may go red, so per-boundary is the simplification that is safe to apply now. About 45 of 191 main commits were refreshes, pushes ~10 min apart.

Ask the user to keep the WSL2 host awake: 13.6 h (24.10 11:40Z to 25.10 01:17Z, launcher 'not moved' with heartbeat-predates-boot restart) exceeds all suite repeats combined; outside the batch's control, recorded as a request.

KEEP batch-boundary, ownership fence, single owner and serial landing; reconcile every transferred job before any refill; the launcher deadline repair stays in its own queued point. 1440 landed without a point boundary and 1.7 h of stall-only journal followed.

KEEP run-wait and STALLED/TIMEOUT handling; treat any running/- hang as STALLED and never re-await it. Simplify, not extend: declare delegated leases at the known suite duration (119 min full LARGE, 55 min polish pass) in the existing declaration field instead of 45 min, and carry command, SHA and backend in the same declaration across boundaries. Confirm in the cycle that the 4.0 h of WebGPU hangs no longer occur after 1446.

KEEP unchanged: land-point.mjs, local browser tier suites, picture check on both backends where isBackendSensitivePath applies, cross-vendor review, exact pushed-SHA receipts and local Vitest (cloud-clone-only Vitest reds exist, parked 24.10 06:25). Cloud green never stands in; pre-acceptance work is repeated only when its evidence is missing or invalidated.
KEEP author-routing-core ('verification is the work'): cloud authors only first implementations; picture fix loops stay local.

The single 'what runs where' command is batch-in-flight --status, listing cloud session ids, local agents, suites, point, purpose, stage and owner; commission-guard --status stays the pool view. Resolution: batch-in-flight already holds per-job declarations, while commission-guard counts branches and cannot see a session before its branch appears. Both outputs are absent from the material; if a field is missing, extend only the existing declaration fields, with Vitest.

Measured cycle: after landing, run batch-standstill-report.mjs over the next 5 landed points or 48 h, whichever is later, against the baseline 3.37 h per landed point excluding host-down (game points 5.0 h, process points 1.8 h); record per point the cloud sessions active during acceptance, where each delegation ran, waiting successors and repeats. Success is a lower mean per distinct landed point; otherwise name the class that absorbed the gain. One cycle is observation, not causal proof, and carry-in (1297 484 h, 1333 124 h branch age) is excluded from authoring time.
KEEP launcher stalled-no-progress as telemetry but do not count process-exit events as session loss in measurements (see A23).

No code change to batch-in-flight-core refill: the written bound (1 cloud author, 1 waiting successor) supersedes any fill-to-cap wording, and the cap is a ceiling, not a target. The excerpt is TRUNCATED, so whether the core actually commissions automatically is unknown; revisit only after reading the full file.

Vitest in the same change for any decision logic actually modified (author-delegate locality under cloud-switch ON, a batch-in-flight status field); none for procedural rules. Prefer none, per the infrastructure freeze.
